construct.diagnosis_or_process: Lipoid congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to STAR dysfunction
construct.mechanism: STAR normally mediates the rate-limiting transfer of cholesterol into mitochondria for steroidogenesis. Severe STAR deficiency causes profound reduction of adrenal and gonadal steroids; compensatory trophic stimulation drives cholesterol accumulation and progressive steroidogenic-cell injury.
construct.primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination

source_verification.claim: Identifies STAR as the regulator of mitochondrial cholesterol import, explains the two-hit lipid-accumulation model, and describes global steroid deficiency, elevated ACTH/renin, and enlarged lipid-laden adrenals.

second_answer_attack.resolution: Both can impair sex-steroid production in a 46,XY infant, but 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency causes deoxycorticosterone-mediated hypertension and hypokalemia. This infant has global adrenal steroid failure, salt-wasting shock, and lipid-rich enlarged adrenals characteristic of STAR-related lipoid CAH.
